title: Cross-species machine learning identifies transcription factors that negatively regulate plant nitrogen-use efficiency
summary: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost and GENIE3 analyses of conserved nitrogen-response expression patterns prioritized transcription factors associated with nitrogen-use efficiency in Arabidopsis and maize. Loss-of-function tests found higher NUE in Arabidopsis myb33 and tcp2 mutants under both low- and high-nitrogen conditions, and in six other tested TF mutants specifically under low nitrogen; a maize nfya3 mutant also showed higher nitrogen-use efficiency under sufficient nitrogen in field tests.
ai_technology: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost models and GENIE3 random-forest gene-regulatory-network inference
organization: New York University; Purdue University and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

evidence.tested: Loss-of-function tests found higher NUE in Arabidopsis myb33 and tcp2 mutants under both low- and high-nitrogen conditions, and in six other tested TF mutants specifically under low nitrogen; a maize nfya3 mutant also showed higher nitrogen-use efficiency under sufficient nitrogen in field tests.
evidence.unknown: The machine-learning prediction scores are not themselves causal evidence; this paper adds functional evidence from specific mutants. Some tested maize candidate roles were assessed through Arabidopsis homologs, and the maize NFYA3 phenotype described here was under sufficient-N field conditions, not a general yield benefit across conditions.
evidence.ai_role: The models ranked conserved nitrogen-responsive genes and transcription factors for contribution or network connectivity to NUE; researchers selected the candidates and tested loss-of-function mutants in Arabidopsis and maize, including field-grown maize.
